column1: # The same questions, phrased the way a person types them.
# DRAFTED BY CLAUDE, NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE OWNER. Every row is a rewrite of a
# row in queries.tsv with the SAME expected answer — only the wording moves,
# toward how somebody actually asks: articles, auxiliaries, "how do I", "is
# there anything that", "which one of these". The rule from queries.tsv still
# holds and matters more here: a query must never contain its own answer's name.
# Why the band exists: M12b's stopword defect was found by an anecdote, because
# no labeled query was phrased this way and the eval was structurally unable to
# see a fault that only natural phrasing triggers. Scored as its own row
# (`contour:natural`) so it can never flatter, or be flattered by, the headline.
# What it is NOT: a second opinion on the same 22 questions. The expected answers
# are identical by construction, so a gap between this row and `contour` is a
# fact about PHRASING and nothing else — which is the one thing the headline
# cannot tell you.
is there anything that tells me a customer owes us money
which bills has a client not settled yet
how do I record that a bill was paid
what is it that adds up what a bill comes to
how can I tell if this bill is past its due date
where do I find what a buyer still has to pay
how do I check a password against the one that is stored
is there something that stops a person from signing in
what tells me whether this user can still sign in
how do I get a full name for showing to a person
what should I call to validate a bearer token
is there a way to end a login early
how much space is it that a shape encloses
what is the distance around the outside of a shape
how do I get the middle point of a shape
which one of these retries a few times before it gives up
is there anything that waits longer after each failed attempt
what is the thing that is computed once and remembered for later calls
which of these is safe for me to call twice with the same result
how do I hold some stock for a customer before they check out
is there something that says how many units can still be sold
what do I use to add more units to a shelf
